Ai, you're asking me about this year's plan. Let me think it through like I do every spring when I sit with my old lady and go over what we have to do.

**My situation this year.** I'm 67. My back hurts in the mornings. The old lady is 64 and her knees are bad. Our oldest son is in Handan at a construction job — he comes back for wheat harvest in June and cotton picking in October, that's it. Daughter-in-law is at the garment factory in town, she helps on weekends. The two grandkids are in school, they can't do much, maybe pick cotton a few afternoons. So really it's two old people and some help at the busy times. This is why I can't take on anything fancy.

**My land.** 16.1 mu total. About 10 mu I do wheat-maize double crop like most people in the village — it's what the land is set up for, it's what I know. The other 6.1 mu I keep in cotton. My father grew cotton on that piece, the soil over there is a bit sandier, doesn't hold water as well, and cotton does alright on it. Also the government subsidy for cotton helps a little and my neighbor Old Zhang keeps telling me to stay with cotton.

**Wheat (already in the ground since last October).** I planted about 10 mu of Jimai variety — I bought certified seed, around 3 yuan per jin, used maybe 30 jin per mu. Before planting I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu (that 15-15-15 stuff, 40 kg bag, cost me about 130 yuan a bag). Now it's spring, wheat is greening up. Around jointing I'll topdress urea — about half a bag per mu, so 20 kg urea. That's maybe 13 kg nitrogen total per mu if I count it all. My neighbor's boy who went to agricultural school told me that's about right, maybe a bit low, but fertilizer is expensive this year and I can't throw money at it.

Irrigation for wheat: I'll water at green-up if it stays dry, then at jointing, and one more at grain filling. Three times usually. Pumping costs me about 40-50 yuan per mu each time with the electric well. If we get good rain I'll skip one. I pray for rain — saves me money.

For weeds I spray one time at spreading tillers, the 2,4-D stuff, cheap. Aphids I'll watch for, if I see them bad I'll spray once.

I'm hoping for about 420 kg per mu. Last year I got 440, year before 400. Depends on the weather in May, if it's hot and dry at grain filling we lose yield.

**Maize (plant right after wheat harvest, around June 15).** Same 10 mu. As soon as the combine leaves the field I have to get the maize seed in — maybe 3-4 days window. No time to plow properly, I do no-till with a seeder my son-in-law's uncle owns, I pay him 40 yuan per mu for planting. Zhengdan or Denghai hybrid seed, whatever the seed store has, about 50 yuan per mu.

Fertilizer for maize: base of compound when I plant, about one bag per mu again, then topdress urea at big trumpet stage — that's when the plant shoots up — maybe 25 kg urea per mu. Total nitrogen around 15-16 kg per mu. Maize eats more nitrogen than wheat in my experience.

Irrigation: usually one or two times, at tasseling if it's dry. If the summer rains come good I don't irrigate at all — last year I only watered once.

Pesticide: one spray for corn borer, sometimes armyworm if neighbors report it.

Hoping for 500 kg per mu. Maize has been good to me lately.

**Cotton (6.1 mu, plant late April).** This is the harder crop. I start the seedbed in early April under plastic, transplant around late April when the soil warms up. Seed cost about 50 yuan per mu. Mulch film adds another 30 yuan per mu.

Fertilizer: cotton is finicky. I put base compound at planting, about 35 kg per mu, then side-dress urea twice — once at squaring, once at flowering. Total nitrogen maybe 13 kg per mu. I don't overdo it because too much nitrogen and the plant grows tall but makes no bolls — my father taught me that.

Irrigation: twice usually, at squaring and at peak flowering. Cotton doesn't like wet feet.

Pesticide: this is where cotton eats money. Aphids, spider mites, bollworm — I spray maybe 5-6 times through the season. I buy cheaper Chinese products, not the expensive ones. Maybe 150 yuan per mu in pesticide altogether.

Labor: cotton picking is the killer. Three or four picks from September to October. My hands hurt. I'll get the old lady, my son when he comes back, daughter-in-law on weekends, grandkids for a few afternoons. Might have to hire two or three days of help at 100 yuan a day per person if we fall behind.

Expecting maybe 240 kg lint per mu. Prices have been so-so. If cotton prices stay low next year I might think about switching those 6 mu to maize too, but for now I stay with cotton.

**Tradeoffs I'm making.** I'm under-fertilizing a little compared to what the extension guy says, because I don't have the cash and I'd rather lose a little yield than not have money for my grandson's school fees. I'm keeping cotton even though it's labor-heavy because the land suits it and I'm too old to learn something new. I'm relying on family labor at the peaks because hired hands are 100 yuan a day and that adds up fast.
